chapter.title: The present subjunctive and the past subjunctive

grammar_rules.title: Formation of the present subjunctive and irregular stems
grammar_rules.explanation:
Find the stem from ils/elles present (ils parl-ent, ils finiss-ent, ils vend-ent). Add endings: que je -e, que tu -es, qu'il -e, que nous -ions, que vous -iez, qu'ils -ent.
Irregular stems:
- être: sois, sois, soit, soyons, soyez, soient
- avoir: aie, aies, ait, ayons, ayez, aient
- faire: fass-
- aller: aill- / all-
- pouvoir: puiss-
- savoir: sach-
- vouloir: veuill- / voul-

steps: Nous and vous use 'nous' present stem for stem-changing verbs

exceptions: être, avoir, faire, aller, pouvoir, savoir, vouloir are irregular

common_mistakes.explanation: Faire uses stem fass- in subjunctive.

grammar_rules.title: Subjunctive after verbs of necessity, will, and desire
grammar_rules.summary: Use subjunctive after il faut que, vouloir que, désirer que, exiger que, demander que.
grammar_rules.explanation: When two different subjects are involved and the main clause expresses a command, wish, or necessity: 'Il faut que tu viennes' (You must come); 'Je veux qu'elle parte' (I want her to leave).
usage_conditions: Two different subjects with expressing will/necessity
exceptions: Espérer que takes indicative (J'espère qu'il viendra), not subjunctive.

grammar_rules.title: Conjunctions that always require the subjunctive
grammar_rules.summary: bien que, quoique (although), pour que, afin que (so that), avant que (before), sans que (without), à condition que (on condition that), pourvu que (provided that), jusqu'à ce que (until).
grammar_rules.explanation:
These conjunctions introduce clauses expressing concession, purpose, condition, or anticipation and always trigger the subjunctive:
- 'Bien qu'il pleuve, nous sortirons' (Although it's raining, we will go out).
- 'Je t'explique pour que tu comprennes' (I'm explaining so that you understand).
usage_conditions: Subordinate clauses with special adverbial conjunctions
exceptions: après que takes indicative, though spoken French often confuses it.

common_mistakes.explanation: Bien que always requires the subjunctive.

usage_notes: Most common trigger of the subjunctive in French

examples.french: Il faut que nous fassions attention.
examples.english: We must be careful / It is necessary that we be careful.

Bien qu'il soit malade, il continue à travailler.
